profile.research_note: Hyperscaler carve-out: portfolio-level facts only. Meta's own locations page lists 28 named US campuses (list captured below) but does not state a single aggregate US or global data center count, nor MW capacity or dollar investment totals; none of those aggregate figures were located elsewhere this session.

reading:
Meta Platforms, Inc. is a public company trading as META, SEC filer CIK 1326801, headquartered in Menlo Park, California. Its data center infrastructure is documented on a dedicated operator site, datacenters.atmeta.com, separate from its consumer product domains.

That site names 28 US data center campuses across 23 states as of this research session, spanning long-established sites such as Prineville, Oregon and Forest City, North Carolina to newer named locations including Temple, Texas, Kansas City, Missouri, and Cheyenne, Wyoming. The page does not state a single aggregate US or global data center count, nor a megawatt capacity figure or dollar-denominated investment total, so no portfolio-scale figure comparable to AWS's disclosed Virginia spending could be recorded for Meta this session.

The registry here tracks 53 Meta facilities across thirteen states, Alabama, Georgia, Iowa, Missouri, North Carolina, Nebraska, New Mexico, Ohio, Oregon, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, and Virginia, a subset of the 23-state footprint named on Meta's own site, which additionally lists campuses in Arizona, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, South Carolina, and Wisconsin not reflected among this registry's current Meta rows.

Meta's campus naming pattern, small towns and counties such as Richland Parish, Louisiana and Sarpy, Nebraska rather than major metro cores, mirrors Google's rural and semi-rural site selection more than AWS's or Digital Realty's metro-clustered model, a pattern this registry's later facility-level research can test against local economic-development or utility-filing records for each named campus.
